There are exactly $e$ partitions $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_e$ of $n$ with $e$-core $\gamma$; list them in dominance order, $\lambda_1\rhd\lambda_2\rhd\cdots\rhd\lambda_e$. Moreover exactly $\lambda_1$ is not $e$-restricted, while $\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_e$ are. Under the Schur functor ([[thm-schur-functor-sends-weyl-and-simple-modules-to-specht-and-hecke-simple-modules]]) the corresponding Murphy Specht classes are $$[S^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_2}_{\mathrm M}],\qquad [S^{\lambda_k}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_k}_{\mathrm M}]+[D^{\lambda_{k+1}}_{\mathrm M}]\ (2\le k<e),\qquad [S^{\lambda_e}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_e}_{\mathrm M}],$$ with $D^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}=0$; conjugating partitions and applying the same $\theta$ pullback to both modules ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]], [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]) gives the corresponding decomposition matrix for the page's Dipper-James Specht modules in $e$-regular labels.
